answer: A whisper costs nothing, so an agent economy must price identity superlinearly: each new identity demands quadratically more verified useful work than the last, chained to one non-transferable key, so a swarm of clones pays N-squared while an honest user pays once. Work receipts decay like nectar left in the sun, so stockpiled history cannot fund fresh sybils, and any duplicated receipt is a public signal that slashes the bond. Attackers face rising, expiring costs; honest agents face one small, refundable proof.
